title: Quadratic regression
intro: At x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 the readings are 10.25, 15, 19.5, 15, 10.25 in order. Fit a quadratic. Predict at x = 1.5; compare the fitted and observed maxima.

beats.spoken: Start with two named columns. Each row is one paired observation.
beats.coach: Lists xval and yval are already named. Keep every predictor and its matching response on the same row.

beats.spoken: In Lists and Spreadsheet, choose Statistics, Stat Calculations, then Quadratic Regression.
beats.coach: Menu → 4 Statistics → 1 Stat Calculations → 6 Quadratic Regression.

beats.spoken: Use the right arrow and Tab to choose the lists x val for X and y val for Y.
beats.coach: From X List: Right to open; Tab confirms xval and moves to Y. Right to open Y, Right again to select yval, then Tab.

beats.spoken: Store the fit to f one. Keep each pair once and the results in C. Press Enter.
beats.coach: Check store to f1, Frequency List 1 and results in C. Press Enter to calculate.

beats.spoken: Read a, b and c in order. R squared summarises this fit; it is not another coefficient in the equation.
beats.coach: Read a = −2, b = 8 and c = 10: f₁(x) = −2x² + 8x + 10. R² describes fit to these readings; it is not a coefficient or a prediction guarantee.

beats.spoken: Predict at x equals one point five by substituting it into the fitted equation, not reading a nearby data row.
beats.coach: Substitute x = 1.5: −2(1.5)² + 8(1.5) + 10 = 17.5 exactly. A measured row is not a model prediction.

beats.spoken: The curve bends down. Its vertex lies inside the observed interval and is higher than both endpoints.
beats.coach: The fitted curve opens down. Its vertex x = −b/(2a) = 2 is inside [0, 4], and f₁(2) = 18.

beats.spoken: At x equals two the recorded value was nineteen point five. The fitted curve predicts eighteen there. The model need not pass through any observation.
beats.coach: At x = 2, the highest measured y is 19.5 but the model peaks at 18. The recorded value is 1.5 above the fitted value, even at the same x.
